name: Agent rapidly created and published by an unapproved maker
description: Successful creation followed within 30 minutes by publication of the same observed BotId by the same UPN in the same environment, without an enabled matching maker approval. Includes unregistered agents; inventory enriches registration status only.
limitations: Requires validated observed BotId payload, a UPN-valued ActorName, environment ID and event UID, but not inventory registration. Inventory is left-joined for Registered/Unknown status only; missing inventory watchlist remains a setup failure. Different creator/publisher, missing fields, partial successes and failed operations are excluded. Approval is evaluated at query time, not historical event time. Exact event linkage is not malicious intent; no ATT&CK tactic asserted.

name: Registered agent authentication configuration changed
description: Successful Copilot Studio BotAuthUpdate on a known enabled agent; reports configuration change without asserting weakened authentication.
limitations: Operation name alone cannot establish old/new authentication mode, weakened controls or an attacker. Requires BotId in validated Properties or PropertyCollection object and event UID. ActorUPN is empty when ActorName is not a UPN. No ATT&CK tactic asserted.

name: Permission assignment audit targets a registered agent identity
description: Successful Entra app-role assignment or delegated permission grant audit whose ServicePrincipal target ID matches an enabled agent inventory identity; a configuration review signal, not an escalation claim.
limitations: Known object ID match is required; never matches display name or app ID to an object ID. TargetResources may include resource and client principals: targeting does not identify the grantee or prove risky permissions. Validate audit target shape and operation spelling locally. No privileged scope classification or ATT&CK tactic asserted.

name: Registered agent identity signs in after a permission audit
description: Permission audit targeting a known agent service principal followed within 30 minutes by a successful service-principal sign-in with the same object ID.
limitations: Uses exact service-principal object ID and bounded time, but audit targeting may mean resource rather than grantee. Sign-in proves authentication only, not use of the new permission, API access, sensitive-data access or escalation. ActorUPN refers to the audit initiator, not the signing-in service principal. Managed identity sign-ins are not covered.

name: Registered agent runtime spawns a shell with network activity
description: A registered endpoint runtime directly creates a selected shell or script host, followed within 10 minutes by a successful connection from that exact child process instance.
limitations: Device ID plus case-insensitive exact parent filename/path identifies a configured runtime, not a proven agent session. Child/network linkage additionally requires PID and exact creation time to avoid PID reuse. Covers selected direct Windows shell children only; ordinary administrative tools can trigger. A connection does not prove exfiltration. Execution tactic maps observed shell execution, not a verified attack.

name: Registered agent runtime contacts a new non-allowlisted destination
description: Successful runtime connection to a hostname absent from both the enabled per-agent allowlist and the preceding observable portion of a 14-day baseline; requires at least three observed baseline days.
limitations: Requires nonempty valid enabled allowlist per agent, hostname-bearing RemoteUrl, and baseline observations on three distinct days. Recent window is one hour; baseline is earlier observations within 14 days, not first-ever access. Hostname equality only, no suffix/wildcard approval. Does not cover IP-only events, prove data transfer, or claim MDE observes arbitrary file reads. No ATT&CK tactic asserted.

name: Optional: injection signal followed by a successful agent action
description: Normalized custom injection signal followed strictly later within 10 minutes by a successful tool invocation or external submission in the same registered agent session.
limitations: Not native Microsoft telemetry. Requires schema 1.0 contract and producer-guaranteed unique sessions and immutable event IDs. Ordered session association does not prove prompt influence or malicious action. Blocked, failed and unknown actions are excluded; equal timestamps cannot establish order. No ATT&CK mapping inferred for prompt injection.

name: Optional: sensitive-data access followed by a non-allowlisted tool submission
description: Successful normalized Confidential or HighlyConfidential data access followed strictly later within 10 minutes by successful external tool submission in the same agent, session and nonempty correlation context.
limitations: Not native telemetry. Requires trusted classifications, a nonempty correlation ID linking the trace, tool name, canonical destination hostname and an enabled per-agent allowlist. Excludes blocked/failed/unknown operations. Shared trace does not prove the submitted bytes contain the accessed data or establish exfiltration; no ATT&CK tactic asserted.
